name: gst-registration
description: When a supplier must register under GST: the turnover limits in CGST Act section 22 and its notifications, compulsory registration for inter-State supplies (section 24(i)), the exemption for small suppliers of inter-State services, and the rule that an export is an inter-State supply. Turnover limits are on aggregate turnover in a financial year, which includes exports.

sources.title: CGST Act, 2017, section 22 (persons liable for registration), as amended
sources.notes: ₹20 lakh; ₹10 lakh from special category States (first proviso); Explanation (iii): special category States are those in article 279A(4)(g) except Jammu and Kashmir, Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Himachal Pradesh, Meghalaya, Sikkim and Uttarakhand, which leaves Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland and Tripura.

sources.title: CGST Act, 2017, section 24 (compulsory registration in certain cases)
sources.notes: Clause (i): persons making any inter-State taxable supply must register notwithstanding section 22(1).

sources.title: CGST Act, 2017, section 2(6) (aggregate turnover)
sources.notes: Aggregate value of taxable supplies, exempt supplies, exports of goods or services and inter-State supplies of persons with the same PAN, on an all-India basis, excluding the taxes.

sources.title: IGST Act, 2017, section 7(5) (inter-State supply)
sources.notes: A supply where the supplier is in India and the place of supply is outside India is an inter-State supply. So an export of services falls under section 24(i) unless an exemption applies.

sources.title: Notification 10/2017-Integrated Tax, 13 October 2017
sources.notes: Exempts persons making inter-State supplies of taxable services from registration if their aggregate turnover, on an all-India basis, does not exceed ₹20 lakh in a financial year; ₹10 lakh for special category States (proviso).

sources.title: Notification 10/2019-Central Tax, 7 March 2019 (in force 1 April 2019)
sources.notes: Exempts persons engaged exclusively in the supply of goods with aggregate turnover up to ₹40 lakh, except persons who must register under section 24, suppliers of ice cream, pan masala and tobacco (2105 00 00, 2106 90 20, chapter 24), persons making intra-State supplies in Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur, Meghalaya, Mizoram, Nagaland, Puducherry, Sikkim, Telangana, Tripura and Uttarakhand, and persons who opt to register voluntarily.

sources.title: Recommendations of the 57th GST Council meeting, 8 October 2026 (PIB press release)
sources.notes: Checked for changes to the registration limits: none recommended. It recommends export-of-services and registration process reforms that do not change who must register.

entries.rule: Supplier of services, or of goods and services: must register when aggregate turnover in the financial year exceeds this limit.
entries.states: all except the special category States

entries.rule: Same, for a supplier in a special category State.
A person making any inter-State taxable supply must register whatever the turnover, unless an exemption notification applies.
A supply by a supplier in India with place of supply outside India (an export) is an inter-State supply.
Persons making inter-State supplies of taxable services are exempt from registration while aggregate turnover, all-India, does not exceed this limit; a lower limit applies in special category States.
entries.note: limit and limit_special are from the official 2017 text. Which States get the lower limit was changed by Notification 3/2019-Integrated Tax (listed on https://cbic-gst.gov.in/hindi/integrated-tax.html), whose official text could not be opened on 2026-11-24; for a supplier in a north-eastern or hill State, confirm with a CA.

entries.rule: Aggregate turnover counts exports, exempt supplies and inter-State supplies, all-India, excluding GST.
Supplier exclusively of goods: exempt up to this limit, except the listed goods, persons covered by section 24, and intra-State suppliers in the listed States (who fall back to section 22's limits).

not_covered: Which States get the ₹10 lakh limit in the inter-State services exemption after Notification 3/2019-Integrated Tax (official text not opened).
Inter-State supplies of goods by small suppliers: no general exemption was verified here, so section 24(i) is shown as applying; check special exemptions (for example handicraft goods) with a CA.
Goods suppliers in Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland and Tripura: whether a notification under section 22's second proviso raised their ₹10 lakh limit was not verified.
The other categories in section 24 (reverse charge, e-commerce sellers, agents, casual and non-resident taxable persons, TDS deductors, input service distributors).
